claim: C+ is NOT Rust-equivalent; statuses describe evidence, not guarantees

gates.name: static array bounds
gates.mechanism: C+ front-end token-level [CPLUS-BOUNDS]/[CPLUS-SAFE-BOUNDS] rejection of constant indices on same-function arrays; __builtin_object_size(p,1) object extents for checked copy APIs. No C+ mechanism for interprocedural, pointer-parameter or heap-capacity bounds.
gates.limitation: Only constant/direct subscripts are rejected. A heap destination such as malloc(1) indexed in a loop compiles silently and corrupts the heap; raw pointer parameters are not bounds-checked.

gates.name: runtime bounds
gates.mechanism: Checked _s APIs and the ordinary-C mapping use tracked remaining capacity (interior and one-past-end pointers) plus __builtin_object_size(p,1), with strict fail-closed mode. Raw runtime-indexed subscripts are detected only by Clang UBSan, not by C+.
gates.limitation: No C+ runtime instrumentation for raw array subscripts. UBSan abort is sanitizer evidence, not a language guarantee; default mode warns but does not refuse when capacity is genuinely unknown.

gates.name: heap alloc/dealloc safety
gates.mechanism: Side-table allocation metadata with generation counters, overflow-rejecting calloc/realloc, live-count telemetry, checked free. ASan observes host malloc blocks but is verification only.
gates.limitation: Raw p[i] on a tracked heap block is not checked; cross-allocator free and host-free bypass are undefined behaviour; metadata is diagnostic rather than provenance. ASan OOB reports are sanitizer evidence.

gates.name: use-after-free
gates.mechanism: Explicit cplus_check_live / cplus_alloc_is_live, generation checks, checked release, and caller-side re-derivation of aliases after realloc; fail-stop on detected stale handles.
gates.limitation: A stale raw alias cannot be revoked; a recycled address can defeat the bounded recent-free table; the dedicated test calls the check explicitly and does not make arbitrary dereferences safe.

gates.name: double free
gates.mechanism: cplus_free_checked / free_checked_s with an open-addressed recent-free cache refuse repeated or invalid release; deterministic C+ runtime traps.
gates.limitation: Classification is best-effort with a 1024-entry cache; collisions can misclassify. Raw free(p) twice and wrong-allocator frees remain undefined behaviour.

gates.name: ownership/lifetime
gates.mechanism: C+ resource/owner/borrow annotations with compile-time move, copy, escape and stack-return diagnostics; ownership-transfer and generation APIs plus explicit caller discipline.
gates.limitation: 547 of 1200 stack-escape scenarios are undiagnosed; no dedicated [CPLUS-LIFETIME] stack-escape check, no interprocedural lifetime analysis, and no borrow checker for raw C (explicitly out of scope).

gates.name: null/dangling
gates.mechanism: Compile-time null-dereference diagnostics for provable cases; guarded library entry points set errno=EINVAL and return defined failures; liveness/generation queries for tracked pointers.
gates.limitation: Unguarded ISO APIs intentionally keep UB; escaped raw pointers and compound-literal addresses cannot be revoked; null pointer parameters to a helper escape some checks.

gates.name: data races
gates.mechanism: One C+ compile-time diagnostic for unsynchronized writes to a shared global; atomics/mutexes inside allocator and logging metadata; caller-side mutex and stop flag in the safe scenario.
gates.limitation: The cve-like race fix is caller-side and TSan output is sanitizer evidence; no language-level thread-ownership model, and shared FILE*, errno and mbstate_t remain caller synchronization responsibility.

gates.name: integer overflow
gates.mechanism: calloc/realloc reject wrapping n*size; conversion wrappers saturate with ERANGE; C+ compile-time diagnostics for some shift counts; checked arithmetic guards in safe scenario variants. Signed-overflow runtime detection is UBSan only.
gates.limitation: Signed overflow, divide-by-zero and invalid shifts are NOT FIXABLE BY LIBC; the runtime test is UBSan. Unsigned wrap is well-defined and not flagged. Rust release builds wrap by default unless overflow-checks are enabled.

gates.name: uninitialized memory
gates.mechanism: Dedicated C+ compile-time diagnostics for locally provable uninitialized reads; corpora use deliberately hostile but initialized objects so wrappers define their behaviour.
gates.limitation: Reading truly uninitialized memory, or an uninitialized field of an otherwise initialized object, is caller UB; no language-level definite-assignment analysis for all paths.

gates.name: function-pointer/indirect-call validation
gates.mechanism: C+ [CPLUS-BOUNDS] rejects a constant out-of-range index into a function-pointer table; caller-side cmd<N check in the safe variant. Runtime index detection is Clang UBSan only.
gates.limitation: C+ inserts no runtime check for an index it cannot prove statically; no CFI, indirect-call target validation or shadow stack, so a corrupted table would still be followed.

gates.name: FFI/unsafe boundaries
gates.mechanism: Explicit header opt-in for ordinary-C mapping, typed checked APIs and machine-readable contracts with stated limitations; these are conventions and contracts, not a language-enforced boundary.
gates.limitation: No unsafe keyword or language-enforced FFI boundary; C+ cannot establish provenance or interior-object identity for arbitrary pointers, cannot prevent cross-allocator frees, and cannot make a host call safe.
